Consult Summary:
- Patient with 1-week history of sore throat progressing to a dry cough and mild exertional shortness of breath; advised supportive care and provided a sick note.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Sore throat for ~1 week, followed by dry cough 1–2 days later. Cough not worse at night.
- Associated symptoms: Exertional shortness of breath began ~3–4 days ago (after cough), unusual but not limiting normal activities; intermittent headaches (now resolved); transient fever for first ~3 days (resolved); decreased appetite without reported weight loss.
- Pertinent negatives: No sputum production; no hemoptysis; no nasal/sinus congestion; no rashes. Conflicting statements about chest pain (see Quality checks).
- Past medical history: None reported. No history of asthma. No history of clots.
- Medications: None currently.
- Allergies: Peanuts. No medication allergies reported.
- Family history: Mother had lung cancer. No known family history of clots.
- Social history: Non-smoker (reports only trying smoking once or twice). Unknown asbestos exposure. Born in the US; living in the UK for ~12 years; recent travel only within Europe.

Examination:
- Vitals: Not recorded.
- Findings: No in-person exam performed. Patient reports no palpable neck lumps.

Impression:
- Acute sore throat and dry cough with mild exertional shortness of breath; likely self-limiting viral upper respiratory tract infection. Low concern for tuberculosis or lung cancer if symptoms improve as expected.

Plan:
- Supportive care: Paracetamol; maintain adequate fluids; rest. (Dose/route/frequency not documented.)
- Work: Sick note provided for a few more days off work.
- Safety-netting:
  - Seek in-person GP assessment if symptoms significantly worsen, if shortness of breath increases or changes suddenly, or if patient becomes concerned.
  - If not improving within 4–5 days, re-contact a healthcare professional.

Quality checks:
- Missing expected elements: No vitals (temperature, respiratory rate, SpO2) or physical exam of throat/chest; no COVID-19 status/testing discussed; medication dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Internal conflicts: Patient initially denied shortness of breath, then reported exertional shortness of breath (conflict noted). Patient affirmed “a bit” of wheeze and chest pain, but later the clinician stated the patient did not have chest pain (conflict noted).
- Transcript quality: Generally understandable; some interruptions/overlap and minor inaudible or truncated segments.
